newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says signs 23 oil deals with foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says signs 23 oil deals with foreign firms.

text.p: Iraq has signed 23 oil contracts with foreign firms to sell oil under an "oil-for-food" deal signed with the United Nations, a senior Iraqi oil official said on Thursday.

"The Oil Ministry has signed 23 contracts to buy Iraqi crude with 23 companies to be implemented in three months time under the memorandom of understanding signed with the United Nations," Saddam Zeban Hassan, chairman of the State Organisation for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) told the Iraqi News Agency.
He did not disclose the names of the firms but said they were Russian, Spanish, American, British, Italian, Japanese and Chinese as well as multi-national companies.
Hassan did not say whether the 23 deals were cleared by the United Nations but said that the Ministry received the U.N. clearance of a number of contracts.
The United Nations said on Friday it had cleared five contracts and had none pending. It had reported some earlier contracts were rejected, but said they could be resubmitted.

Iraq last week began oil exports worth $2 billion over six months under the oil-for-food deal to buy humanitrarian needs for its people, under sweeping trade sanctions imposed since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Hassan said SOMO was conducting talks with other firms to finalise deals in the coming few days.
The sale of Iraqi crude and purchase of urgent humanitarian needs like food and medicine are under strict U.N. monitoring.
